content.heading: Stop pasting requirements into chat
content.body: Name them once. Link them. Hand the model a slice — not the whole repo.

slides.notes: If you work with language models on real projects, you already write requirements — you just write them into the chat window, over and over.

content.heading: Same intent, two shapes
content.body: Prose dumps drift. Named ideas stay findable.
content.code:
Users must log in. Empty passwords fail.
Sessions time out. Failed attempts get logged.
Also remember rate limits somehow…
content.code_b:
login must reject empty passwords
session expires after inactivity
audit_log records failed attempts

slides.notes: reqlan turns that intent into a graph of named ideas — requirements as code.

content.heading: The get-started loop
content.body: Write → link → inspect neighbourhood → ask with a small slice → point at code.

slides.notes: Day one is name, prose, related work — not a ceremony of metadata.

content.heading: Install, then open a folder
content.body: VS Code Marketplace or Open VSX. First launch shows a short welcome.

slides.notes: Keep the welcome links handy; we will use them later.

content.heading: Requirements as code for LLM work
content.body: Owned in git. Searchable. Small enough to paste on purpose.

slides.notes: Next: write your first idea in under a minute.
